subject: Request: Guest access for SOC 2 Type II audit + evidence snapshot
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmepayments.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Guest access for SOC 2 Type II audit + evidence snapshot

Hi Irene,

We're scheduled to begin the SOC 2 Type II review for Acme Payments the week of April 10. Could you provision temporary access for our external auditor group to Redwood's trust portal so they can review controls and download a limited evidence snapshot?

Requested window: Apr 4 09:00 PDT – Apr 6 23:59 PDT (we can compress if needed).
Requested scope (high level):
- SOC 2 report PDF (most recent Type II)
- Selected evidence for the period 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31 per the attached manifest (logs, change approvals, vendor attestations)
- Control owners contact list for follow-up (email + title)

Two questions:
1) Can you provide a one-time SSO link or visitor account (no persistent user) with download rights limited to the requested bundle?
2) If you prefer to push an evidence ZIP to us, can it be a filtered snapshot (we only need the manifest items) and include a checksum manifest?

Attaching our auditor roster and manifest. Please advise next steps and any bridge letter we should sign.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Lead Auditor
Acme Payments Audit Team

Attachments: acme_auditor_roster.csv; requested_manifest.csv
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Guest access for SOC 2 Type II audit + evidence snapshot

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the details 94 we can support both options but prefer issuing a time-boxed visitor role via our Trust Portal for traceability. Quick answers up front:

- We can create a visitor account with one-time SSO (ephemeral link) valid for a 48-hour window.
- Downloads can be scoped to a named evidence bundle; we'll create a filtered snapshot based on your manifest to minimize extraneous data.
- We typically require a bridge letter confirming the audit scope and date range; I've attached our bridge_letter_template.pdf to speed that along.

Two clarifying questions:
1) Can you confirm the exact auditor emails (so we can restrict to those addresses)?
2) Any special controls youd like redacted in advance (e.g., PII in sample data)?

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm auditor emails + accept bridge letter template.
2) We generate the filtered evidence bundle and a one-time SSO link.
3) We share the link and an evidence manifest (sha256 checksums) and leave the visitor access live for the agreed window.

Looping in Marissa from Trust Ops to confirm the export process and Ben for any contract edge cases.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Security & Trust Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridge_letter_template.pdf

Thanks, Irene.

Auditor emails:
- mike.hart@acmepayments.com

No PII redaction required for the artifacts you've listed. The auditors will need – per their internal checklist – the following high-priority items inside the bundle:
- System change approval logs (Jan9Dec 2027)
- Admin access reviews (2027 quarterly snapshots)
- Vendor SOC/attestation docs for critical vendors listed in manifest

We prefer the one-time SSO visitor link approach. Please issue link no later than Apr 4 so the team can validate access before the on-site start on Apr 10.

I'll return a signed copy of the bridge letter by end of day Apr 3.

Best,
Laura
